The company has more than 900 employees, inspired by the shared vision of improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


FLIGHT OPERATIONS

 - Build and maintain the operational meteorological picture before and during the flight, using the available tools (forecast models, radiosondes, lidar and aircraft data), drift planning, and identify weather and terrain-related hazards relevant to the flight profile.

 - Identify suitable launch, flight and recovery windows and communicate them to the flight crew.

 - Develop and maintain the mission plan (route, altitude, speed profile and timing), customer mission goals, integrating weather, airspace, aircraft performance, aircraft health and energy constraints.

 - Continuously assess predicted cut-down and debris impact zones to keep the planned trajectory within the permitted ground impact area.

 - Maintain readiness for degraded operations for a return-to-home mission profile in case re-planning of a return is necessary or in case of the plane entering a degraded operational mode due to a mechanical or electrical servicing need.

 - Monitor aircraft progress against the plan, update it when required, and coordinate mission planning and meteorological decisions with the flight crew and engineering teams.


WIDER OPERATIONS SUPPORT

 - Contribute to the planning, preparation and execution of flight test campaigns, including site preparation, pre-flight checks, launch and recovery activities.

 - Take on other crew positions or ground control station duties as operational needs require, building versatility across the Operations team.

 - Analyse flight data after each flight, report results and translate findings into improvements for the aircraft, its systems and operating procedures.

 - Develop and maintain operational procedures, checklists, emergency procedures and operations documentation.

 - Develop and improve monitoring, analysis and planning tools used by the flight crew, such as telemetry dashboards and energy or thermal estimation tools.

 - Support aircraft integration, ground testing and simulation activities, and contribute to the training and qualification of crew members.

 - Support safety and risk assessments for operations and, when needed, coordination with aviation authorities and external partners.


REQUIREMENTS


MUST HAVE SKILLS

 - 5+ years of relevant experience in UAS or aircraft testing and operations.

 - Good knowledge of meteorology (wind profiles, convection, turbulence, icing, thermal activity, etc.) and the ability to interpret forecast models, synoptic charts and upper-air data.

 - Experience in flight or mission planning, including route, altitude and timing under weather and airspace constraints.

 - Understanding of aircraft performance and of how weather affects flight safety and endurance.

 - Clear communication and the ability to work as part of a flight crew, including during long-endurance operations.

 - Programming or scripting skills for data analysis and tooling (e.g. Python; C/C++) a plus.

 - Ability to drive large vehicles or convoys (within limits of B license).

 - Good command of the English language, both oral and written.


NICE TO HAVE SKILLS

 - Aviation meteorology qualification, or experience as a forecaster or weather briefer for flight operations.

 - Hands-on experience with radiosonde launches, lidar or other atmospheric measurement systems.

 - Experience with airspace management and coordination with ATC.

 - Experience with trajectory, cut-down or debris impact modelling.

 - Experience with solar-powered, electric or long-endurance aircraft, or with high-altitude platforms and balloons.

 - Experience with safety analysis in the SORA framework.

 - Familiarity with GIS tools, autopilot mission planning and ground software like QGroundControl.

 - EASA-valid remote pilot license up to specific category standard scenarios.

 - Proactive can-do attitude and love for aerospace are expected.

WHO WE ARE

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. jobs.descriptionHtml:
• Senior DevOps Engineer – Core Platform Engineering

  • Location: Espoo, Finland / Berlin, Germany

  • Department: Platform & Release Engineering - Engineering

  • Reports to: Infrastructure Engineering Lead

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Hybrid / Office

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO)

Why this role matters:

As a Senior DevOps Engineer, you’ll design and operate the core platform foundations that power ICEYE’s products, enabling secure, scalable, and reliable services across cloud and on-prem environments.

Who We Are

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE’s world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world’s largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy, day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE’s near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring including oil-spill detection, and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.

ICEYE is headquartered in Finland and operates globally across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We have more than 900 employees, united by a shared vision: improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.

Your day-to-day responsibilities

  • Design, operate, and evolve core platform components including Kubernetes, ingress, service mesh, and secrets management

  • Build and maintain reusable infrastructure modules using Terraform across AWS and on-prem environments

  • Define and implement observability standards, including metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and alerting

  • Partner with product teams to guide platform adoption and enable scalable, platform-aligned architectures

  • Automate platform lifecycle processes including provisioning, upgrades, and scaling

  • Improve platform reliability, performance, and security through continuous iteration

  • Support and mentor engineers on best practices in Kubernetes, networking, identity, and observability

  • Reduce operational overhead through tooling, automation, and improved platform abstractions

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

  • 5+ years of experience in DevOps, SRE, or Platform Engineering roles operating production systems

Role Highlights

  • Workplace model: Office

It also exists to catch issues early, fix them at the source and keep the entire build process traceable and unblocked so spacecraft can be assembled and launched with confidence.

Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring (including oil-spill detection), and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.

ICEYE is headquartered in Finland and operates globally across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We have more than 900 employees, united by a shared vision: improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.


Your day-to-day responsibilities

  • Your Day-to-day Responsibilities

    • Perform inspection, assembly, and verification of mechanical subsystems and panel-level assemblies

    • Integrate structural elements including CFRP panels, sandwich structures, and mechanical components

    • Execute panel assembly, including module installation and routing of wiring harnesses (RF, CAN, power, thermal sensors)

    • Ensure subsystem readiness (e.g. antennas, solar panels) through testing and validation procedures

    • Collaborate with Engineering, AIT, and Quality teams to resolve integration issues and improve manufacturability

    • Monitor production progress and proactively escalate blockers to maintain workflow continuity

    • Support root cause analysis and non-conformance resolution

    • Contribute to First Article Inspection (FAI) activities and ensure proper documentation and traceability

    • Perform or support incoming inspection of mechanical and structural components

    • Maintain accurate records in line with aerospace manufacturing and quality standards


    Requirements:

    Must Haves

    • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field

    • 1+ years of hands-on experience in mechanical assembly, inspection, or integration within aerospace or other high-reliability environments

    • Proven experience working with mechanical subsystems and structural assemblies (e.g. panels, brackets, electro-mechanical units)

    • Hands-on experience with composite materials (e.g. CFRP), sandwich structures, solar panels, or precision mechanical components

    • Experience with panel-level integration, including module installation and wiring harness routing/handling

    • Basic understanding of electrical integration principles, including connectors, grounding, and cable types (RF, CAN, power, thermal sensors)

    • Familiarity with manufacturing quality standards, documentation, and traceability requirements

    • Experience supporting root cause analysis and non-conformance resolution

    • Comfortable working in a fast-paced production environment with evolving priorities and deadlines

    • Hands-on mindset with willingness to work on the shop floor and support cross-functional teams directly

    • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate with Production, Engineering, QA, and Planning

    • High level of ownership, attention to detail, and continuous improvement mindset



    Nice To Haves

    • Experience with satellite structures and panel integration, including CFRP panels, sandwich constructions, and RANT assemblies

    • Hands-on experience with full panel assembly, including integration and routing of RF, CAN, power, and thermal sensor cabling

    • Understanding of thermal management and interfaces (e.g. thermal pads, pastes, sensor integration)

    • Experience with incoming inspection of composite and machined parts

    • Knowledge of environmental and mechanical testing (e.g. vibration, shock, thermal vacuum)

    • Familiarity with aerospace standards such as IPC, ECSS, or similar

    • Experience in NewSpace or small satellite production environments

    • Experience working in cleanroom environments and satellite integration flows

    • Familiarity with ERP/MES systems in manufacturing

  • Hiring Manager General Interview

  • Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge

  • Hiring Team Interview

• Manufacturing Technician, Unmanned Aircraft (Fabrication and Integration)
• Location: Valencia, Spain
• Department: HAPS

  • Assembly of large, but very lightweight unmanned aircraft

  • Fabrication of lightweight aircraft structures/components and building CFRP composite parts

  • Development of new assembly, integration and testing processes, and tools for an ultra-light UAV

  • Manufacturing of electronics assemblies and sub-level components (such as cable harness manufacturing and battery manufacturing of state-of-the-art high power density batteries)

  • Transitioning new designs from engineering to manufacturing

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role highlights:

  • Role: Senior Operations Specialist

  • Department: HAPS

  • Location: Valencia, Spain

  • Working type: Hybrid

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)


The Mission of the Senior Operations Specialist

As Senior Operations Specialist on the HAPS program, you will be the driving force behind getting ICEYE's stratospheric electric aircraft safely and successfully into the sky. You will own the development of the full operations infrastructure — hardware, software, and procedures — as well as the planning and execution of flight test campaigns from the ground up. This means interfacing with aviation authorities to secure flight clearances, developing SORA-based safety assessments, operating the aircraft from the ground control station, and translating flight test results into actionable insights that feed back into the aircraft's development. You will sit at the crossroads of engineering and operations, contributing not just to how the aircraft flies, but to how it is built, tested, and continuously improved — helping establish an operations capability that will scale as the program grows.

 
 

Who are we?

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE's world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world's largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy – day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE's near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. ICEYE operates internationally with offices in Finland, Poland, Spain, Japan, the UAE, Greece, Germany, and the US. The company has more than 900 employees, inspired by the shared vision of improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.

 

Day to day responsibilities:

  • Develop and assist ICEYE flight Operations

  • Plan & coordinate flight testing campaigns

  • Develop SORA-based and MET-based site/operational flight feasibility assessments tools

  • Interface with authorities/external entities for coordination & flight clearance

  • Operate unmanned aircraft (from GCS)

  • Assess and report flight testing results

  • Assist in aircraft and operations related documentation development

  • Assist with aircraft components integration & systems ground testing

  • Assist in aircraft and simulation systems development

  • Assist in aircraft prototyping and systems testing

 

Requirements:

Must have skills

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in UAS testing and operation

  • Experience in aircraft prototyping & manufacturing, e.g. mechanical prototyping tools

  • Experience with safety analysis in the SORA framework

  • Good programming skills (C, C++, Python)

  • Ability to drive large vehicles or convoys (within limits of B license)

  • Good command of the English language, both oral and written

 

Nice to have skills

  • Electronics/avionics engineering profile, being able to debug and/or implement quick SW/HW solutions

  • Good knowledge of meteorology sciences (turbulence formation, thermic activity, etc., and how to identify it).

  • Familiarity with Autopilot/GPS stack calibration

  • Familiarity with ground software like QGroundControl

  • Familiarity with lightweight composite airframes

  • EASA-valid remote pilot license up to specific category standard scenarios

  • Proactive can-do attitude and love for aerospace are expected


Application process

  • Talent Acquisition Interview

  • Hiring Manager Interview

  • Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge

  • Hiring Team Interview

  • Offer Decision

  • Act as the primary point of contact for supplier-related quality issues, including non-conformances, deviation requests, and waiver management

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills across suppliers and cross-functional internal teams

  • Ability to drive results and influence decisions without direct authority

  • Structured problem-solving approach with strong analytical thinking skills

  • High level of ownership with a proactive and hands-on working style

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced and evolving environment

  • Ability to travel at least once a month to meet with our suppliers

  • Familiarity with IPC-A-610 Class 3, IPC/WHMA-A-620 Class 3, J-STD-001, and ECSS standards

  • Experience working with ERP systems in production environments

  • Experience in aerospace, defense, automotive, or other high-reliability manufacturing industries

jobs.title: OBC & Comms AIT Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role Highlights:

  • Title: OBC & Comms AIT Engineer

  • Department: Global Manufacturing Organization

  • Reports to: AIT Engineering Team Lead

  • Location: Espoo, Finland

  • Type of Contract: Permanent

  • Working model: On-site

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

About the role ICEYE is seeking an AIT Engineer to own the assembly, integration, and testing of on-board computer and communications subsystems at our Espoo headquarters. This is a hands-on technical role for an engineer with strong expertise in complex electronics and SDR-based communications systems, ready to contribute directly to spacecraft production and mission-critical troubleshooting in a fast-paced, high-cadence environment.

What you will do

  • Serve as the primary technical point of contact for all OBC and Comms issues during manufacturing, integration, and testing

  • Conduct hands-on inspection, verification, and assembly of OBC and Comms subsystems hardware

  • Identify, contain, and drive root cause analysis of non-conformances; implement corrective actions and close feedback loops into design and production processes

  • Contribute to OBC and Comms design reviews, production ramp-up planning, and DFM/DFT improvements

  • Represent AIT Engineering across projects and disciplines, interfacing with design engineers, production leads, and other domain AIT engineers

  • Apply system-level understanding to anticipate integration risks across subsystem interfaces and ensure mission success

  • Produce and maintain technical documentation including test procedures, NCRs, and corrective action records

What you bring
Must have

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in the development, integration, testing, or production of complex electronics and communications systems

  • Deep technical knowledge of electronics engineering and SDR-based communications systems, with system-level understanding across full hardware architectures

  • Demonstrated experience in multidisciplinary engineering environments, including mentoring engineers and technicians and driving cross-functional collaboration

  • Strong track record in DFM and DFT in high-reliability hardware environments

  • Familiarity with integration, verification, configuration management, and production ramp-up processes in complex hardware industries

  • Proactive, hands-on approach to problem-solving including structured root cause analysis

  • Continuous improvement mindset, with the ability to drive reliability and repeatability as production volumes scale

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously

  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills

  • Experience writing clear, traceable technical documentation

Nice to have

  • Experience with issue tracking and configuration management tools

  • Familiarity with Python or AI-assisted tools for productivity and test automation

  • Rapid ability to structure and synthesize complex technical information and communicate conclusions clearly

  • Resilience and sustained motivation in high-pressure production environments

  • Transparency, humility, and an active growth mindset

 

Application Process

  • Talent Acquisition Interview

  • Hiring Manager General Interview

  • Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge

  • Hiring Team + Director-level Interview

  • Offer Decision

What We Offer at ICEYE

At ICEYE, you will join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. We know that we will succeed only through exceptional people in our team, which is why your growth, well-being, and success are a priority.

As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. You will benefit from continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a ICEYE is a place where your contributions have a visible impact and where we celebrate success together.

 

Benefits

  • A job that matters in a dynamic Defence Technology and Earth Observation environment with a scale-up approach

  • An independent role with a supportive and diverse work environment

  • Time for self-development, research, training, conferences, or certification schemes

  • Health insurance

  • Creative, inspiring and collaborative office


Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

At ICEYE, we believe that diversity isn't just a buzzword – it's our greatest asset.

We're committed to fostering an inclusive environment where every voice is not only heard but celebrated. We know that diverse perspectives breed innovation and creativity, which is why we actively seek out individuals from all walks of life, backgrounds, and experiences.

Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table. Join us and be part of a team where differences are not only embraced but cherished, because together, we're stronger.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those who may need workplace adjustments. If you require any specific accommodations or assistance during the recruitment process for any reason, please let us know.

Apply now to start your ICEYE journey, and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at iceye.com

  • Department: Engineering

  • Reports to: Engineering Lead, Orbit Control

  • Workplace model: Office / Hybrid

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO)

Why this role matters:

As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll help keep ICEYE’s world-leading SAR satellite constellation operating safely and reliably. Working in the AOCS domain, you will take technical ownership of Orbit Control software that helps ensure our satellites are exactly where they need to be to fulfil their mission. Your work will directly affect the performance, reliability, and quality of the SAR data ICEYE delivers to customers.

Who We Are

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE’s world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world’s largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy, day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE’s near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring including oil-spill detection, and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.

ICEYE is headquartered in Finland and operates globally across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We have more than 900 employees, united by a shared vision: improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.

Your day-to-day responsibilities

  • Take technical ownership of the Orbit Control codebase, primarily written in Python, ensuring it is robust, maintainable, and operationally reliable

  • Design, implement, test, deploy, and maintain ground segment software to control the orbits of our satellites

  • Build and maintain verification and validation procedures for Orbit Control software in close collaboration with operations teams

  • Debug system anomalies systematically and identify root causes to prevent recurrence

  • Improve telemetry data analysis, processing, visualization, logging, monitoring, and alerting capabilities

  • Collaborate with orbital mechanics experts, mission teams, Staff Engineers, and Engineering Leads to translate operational needs into high-quality software solutions

  • Define and promote strong software engineering practices, including automated testing, CI/CD, and operational monitoring

  • Mentor junior engineers and contribute to the technical direction of the team

Must haves:

  • Proven experience across the full software lifecycle, including designing, building, testing, deploying, and maintaining production software

  • Strong experience with operationally critical or high-reliability software systems

  • Expertise in systematic root-cause analysis, diagnostics, monitoring, and debugging of distributed systems

  • Ability to evaluate technical options rigorously and guide teams toward well-considered engineering decisions

  • Strong understanding of software engineering practices such as automated testing, CI/CD, observability, and operational monitoring

  • Ability to lead complex technical initiatives, mentor engineers, and influence technical direction

  • Strong collaboration and communication skills in cross-functional technical environments

Nice to haves:

  • Experience with Kubernetes or similar orchestration systems

  • Experience working with spacecraft operations, orbital mechanics, AOCS, or mission-critical aerospace systems

  • Experience building tools for telemetry analysis, visualization, logging, alerting, or operational insight

  • Hiring Manager interview (remote)

  • Take-home task and technical interview (remote)

  • On-site Systems Design Workshop

  • On-site Behavioural Interview

  • Help translate engineering requirements into RFQs and supplier evaluations, learning how technical specifications become commercial decisions

  • Monitor deliveries, follow up with suppliers on delays, and keep the team updated on order status

  • More drawn to coordination and management (planning, follow-up, working with suppliers and teams) than to hands-on technical design

  • Able to work under pressure and adapt when priorities and requirements shift

  • Fluent English and Spanish, spoken and written

  • Eligible for an internship agreement (convenio de prácticas) with a university or training institution

  • Some exposure to RFQs, supplier selection, ERP tools or Excel-based tracking

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role highlights:

  • Role: Field Technician (UAV Flight Operations)

  • Department: HAPS

  • Location: Valencia, Spain

  • Working type: Hybrid

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)


The Mission of the Field Technician

As a HAPS Operations Field Technician, you'll play a hands-on role in preparing, executing, and assessing ground and flight testing campaigns for ICEYE's High Altitude Platform System — a large-scale UAV project set to make a real mark on aviation history. You'll be part of a growing, dedicated operations team working on one of the most ambitious unmanned aerial programs in the world, with significant room to grow as the team scales.

 

Who are we?

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE's world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world's largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy – day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE's near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. ICEYE operates internationally with offices in Finland, Poland, Spain, Japan, the UAE, Greece, Germany, and the US. The company has more than 900 employees, inspired by the shared vision of improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.

 

Day to day responsibilities:

  • Perform aircraft setup, flight hardware integration, and field and central maintenance across testing campaigns.

  • Assist with aircraft component integration and systems ground-testing, including support on aircraft prototyping and systems testing activities.

  • Plan and coordinate flight testing campaigns from a technical readiness perspective, ensuring all systems and logistics are prepared for safe and effective execution.

  • Operate and/or pilot unmanned aircraft in a support capacity during testing operations.

  • Assess and report on flight testing results, contributing to continuous improvement of operations and aircraft performance.

  • Assist in the development of aircraft and operations-related documentation.

 

Requirements:

Must have skills

  • 3+ years of experience as a specialist, integration, or field technician in a relevant field (unmanned systems, aircraft, robotics, motorsports, or other high-performance/high-complexity systems).

  • Hands-on experience in aircraft, robot, or motorsports prototyping and manufacturing, including familiarity with mechanical prototyping tools (e.g. 3D printing, CAD) and basic UAV/robot components (actuators, motors, ESCs, autopilot systems, etc.).

  • Demonstrated field operations experience with strong technical aptitude and a practical, problem-solving mindset.

  • Good command of English, both written and spoken.

 

Nice to have skills

  • Experience in unmanned aircraft testing and operation, including familiarity with autopilot/GPS stack calibration and ground software such as QGroundControl.

  • Electronics engineering background with the ability to debug and implement quick software or hardware solutions in the field.

  • Familiarity with lightweight composite structures and airframes.

  • Valid EASA remote pilot licence up to specific category standard scenarios clearance.

  • Good command of Spanish, both written and spoken.

  • Proactive, can-do attitude with a genuine passion for aerospace, robotics, or related fields.


Application process

  • Talent Acquisition Interview

  • Hiring Manager Interview

  • Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge

  • Hiring Team Interview

  • Offer Decision

As a HAPS Operations Field Technician, you'll play a hands-on role in preparing, executing, and assessing ground and flight testing campaigns for ICEYE's High Altitude Platform System — a large-scale UAV project set to make a real mark on aviation history. jobs.title: ISR Operator – ICEYE Japan
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About ICEYE

ICEYE delivers unparalleled persistent monitoring capabilities through its constellation of

Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites. Our solutions enable customers to make informed

decisions by providing actionable insights in near real-time, regardless of weather or lighting

conditions.

About the job

We are seeking an ISR Cell Operator to support Japan-focused operations by coordinating satellite tasking, monitoring incoming SAR data, and delivering timely intelligence to customers and internal stakeholders. This role sits at the intersection of operations, analysis, and customer engagement, ensuring that ICEYE’s capabilities are effectively leveraged to meet mission requirements.

Key Responsibilities

• Mission Coordination & Tasking

◦ Manage and prioritize satellite tasking requests for Japan and surrounding regions

◦ Coordinate with internal mission planning teams to optimize collection schedules

◦ Ensure timely execution of customer requirements

• Real-Time Monitoring & Operations

◦ Monitor ISR workflows and data acquisition in near real-time

◦ Track satellite passes, collection status, and delivery timelines

◦ Respond to time-sensitive or high-priority tasking requests

• Data Interpretation & Reporting

◦ Review SAR imagery and derived products to identify relevant changes or events

◦ Generate concise, actionable reports for customers

◦ Support rapid dissemination of insights during critical situations (e.g., disasters, security events)

• Customer & Stakeholder Engagement

◦ Act as a point of contact for Japan-based customers

◦ Translate operational needs into actionable tasking plans

◦ Provide updates on mission status and product delivery

• Operational Support & Continuous Improvement

◦ Maintain situational awareness of regional events impacting ISR priorities

◦ Contribute to process improvements and operational best practices

◦ Support training and onboarding of new team members

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in Geospatial Intelligence, Remote Sensing, Defense Studies, Engineering, software or related field.

• Experience in ISR operations, geospatial analysis, satellite operations, or similar

environments.

• Familiarity with SAR imagery and/or remote sensing data (preferred)

• Engineering or software background.

• Military or law enforcement experience preferred.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex datasets

• Ability to work in a fast-paced, time-sensitive operational environment

• Native-level proficiency in Japanese with business-level fluency in English required.

• Willingness to work flexible hours or shifts if required

• Must be eligible to obtain a security clearance or an equivalent level of clearance.

• Valid Japanese driver’s license required.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience working with government, defense, or security customers in Japan

• Knowledge of maritime domain awareness, disaster response, or border security operations

• Familiarity with GIS tools (e.g., QGIS, ArcGIS) or imagery analysis platforms

• Prior experience in a 24/7 operations or command center environment

Why Join ICEYE Japan?

• Be part of a cutting-edge space technology company transforming Earth observation

• Work on mission-critical operations with real-world impact (e.g., disaster response, national security)

• Collaborate with a global, highly skilled team

• Opportunity to shape ISR operations in the Japan market

Who We Are

ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent

monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar)

satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality,

latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to

operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defense and intelligence, environmental

monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that

contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1,000

employees across Poland, Spain, Germany, the UK, Australia, Japan, the UAE, Greece,

and the US. We’re a growing international team of builders. Join us.

jobs.title: ISR Cell Operator - Germany
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role highlights:

  • ISR Cell Operator - Germany

  • Location: Berlin, Germany

  • Department: ICEYE Germany

  • Reports to: Head of Intelligence, ICEYE Germany

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: On-site / shift-based

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, and German Ü2/Ü3 where required)

Why this role matters:

 

Be the operational backbone that keeps ICEYE Germany's intelligence delivery running — from the moment a tasking request comes in to the moment actionable insight reaches the customer.

You are the person who ensures satellite collection is coordinated, data is monitored, and customers receive timely, accurate intelligence products. You will work across mission planning, data interpretation, and direct customer engagement — keeping ICEYE Germany's operational tempo high and its output trustworthy. You will also serve as a key interface to Germany-based government and defence customers, translating their operational requirements into executable satellite collection plans.

This is an operational role with real stakes. The intelligence you coordinate and deliver informs decisions in national security, disaster response, and critical infrastructure protection.

 

Who We Are


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

 

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

 

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

 

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.


Your day-to-day responsibilities

 

Run the operations cell. Manage and prioritize satellite tasking requests for Germany and surrounding regions. Coordinate with internal mission planning teams to optimize collection schedules and ensure timely execution of customer requirements.

Own real-time monitoring. Track satellite passes, collection status, and delivery timelines across active missions. Respond to time-sensitive or high-priority tasking requests with speed and precision.

Interpret and report. Review SAR imagery and derived products to identify relevant changes or events. Generate concise, actionable intelligence reports for customers and support rapid dissemination during critical situations — natural disasters, security incidents, and time-critical government requirements.

Engage customers and stakeholders. Act as the primary operational point of contact for Germany-based customers, including government and defence agencies. Translate their mission requirements into executable tasking plans and keep them informed on collection status and product delivery.

Maintain the operational picture. Keep situational awareness of regional events — across Germany and the wider DACH region — that affect ISR priorities and collection planning.

Strengthen the function. Contribute to process improvements, operational best practices, and the onboarding and training of new team members as the cell grows.

What We Measure After Twelve Months

  • Germany-focused tasking requests are executed on time and to customer specification, with no critical gaps in coverage.

  • Customer satisfaction among German government and defence accounts is high, with repeat engagement on priority programmes.

  • Operational processes are documented, repeatable, and resilient to staff changes or surge demand.

  • The ISR cell is capable of supporting classified collection workflows at the classification levels enabled by ICEYE Germany's security posture.

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

  • Experience in ISR operations, geospatial analysis, satellite operations, or a directly comparable operational environment — ideally within the Bundeswehr, a German federal security agency (BND, BfV, Federal Police), or a defence industry context.

  • Familiarity with SAR imagery and remote sensing data, and the ability to interpret complex datasets under time pressure.

  • Knowledge of GIS tools such as QGIS or ArcGIS, or comparable imagery analysis platforms.

  • Background with government, defence, or security customers in Germany or the DACH region, and an understanding of how these organisations task, consume, and act on intelligence products.

  • Experience in a 24/7 operations or command centre environment is a strong advantage.

  • Engineering or software background that supports understanding of data pipelines, collection systems, or geospatial platforms.

  • Eligibility for German security clearance (Sicherheitsüberprüfung Ü2/Ü3) is required. Existing clearance is a significant advantage.

  • Fluent English, with the ability to communicate clearly at both working and customer level. German is beneficial but not a hard criteria.

  • Valid European drivers license B

Application Process

  • Intro conversation with Talent Attraction

  • Hiring manager interview with Head of Intelligence, ICEYE Germany

  • Technical case: a take-home operational planning exercise

  • Cross-functional interviews with Operations Lead ISR, Intelligence Products, and a senior ICEYE leader

  • Final conversation with the CEO, ICEYE Germany

Working at ICEYE

At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.

How We Work (Our Values)

Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.

  • Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.

  • See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.

  • Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

  • Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

  • Have fun: What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing, at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.

 

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

We want ICEYE to be a place where people can be themselves and do great work. Different backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, which is why we work to create an environment where people feel included, respected, and able to speak up. Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table.

We’re committed to fair, inclusive hiring and equal opportunity. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, tell us—we’ll do our best to help.

Apply now to start your ICEYE journey, and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at iceye.com.

  • Location: Espoo, Finland

Why this role matters:

The Harness Manufacturing Technician role is critical to the success of both our ground testing infrastructure and next-generation satellites. By manufacturing high-quality harnesses and evaluating the manufacturability of new cable designs, this role helps ensure reliability, efficiency, and continuous improvement throughout the product development cycle. Cables are the vital interfaces that connect every subsystem, enabling communication, power distribution, and seamless operation across the satellite. As the threads that bring complex systems to life, every harness built contributes directly to mission success.

  • Harness manufacturing for testing setups or satellites

  • Evaluate manufacturability of harness designs and provide feedback to designers

  • Assemble and install wiring harnesses and cable assemblies for satellite systems according to drawings and work instructions.

  • Handle wires, connectors, shielding, and protective coverings with precision and care.

  • Prepare and maintain documentation, traveler sheets, and quality records.

  • Assist in troubleshooting and rework of harness assemblies under supervision.

  • Perform inspections, continuity checks, and basic electrical tests on harness assemblies.

  • Train new joiners and colleagues in harness manufacturing

  • Follow cleanroom and ESD handling procedures.

  • Apply workmanship and quality standards (especially IPC/WHMA-A-620).

What we’re looking for

  • +2 years Hands-on manufacturing experience with electronics assembling and harnesses manufacturing

  • Experience in soldering

  • Familiarity with crimping, soldering, wire stripping, lacing, and connector assembly.

  • Ability to read and interpret assembly drawings, wiring tables, and work instructions.

  • Basic knowledge of workmanship standards such as IPC/WHMA-A-620

  • Fluency in English

  • A positive attitude and a desire to learn new things

  • Previous experience in space, aerospace, or defense harness assembly.

  • Familiarity with coaxial or shielded cable assembly.

  • Exposure to harness testing tools (continuity testers, pull test machines).

jobs.title: Production Reliability Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role highlights:

  • Production Reliability Engineer

  • Location: Athens

  • Department: Mission Assurance & Reliability; Global Manufacturing Organisation

  • Reports to: Manager, Mission Assurance & Reliability

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Office

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO)

Why this role matters:

This role is responsible for assuring the reliability and quality of ICEYE’s subassembly production line, ensuring that assemblies meet design intent, space-grade quality requirements, and operational standards. The Production Reliability Engineer works closely with AIT engineering, production technicians, and integration teams to prevent quality escapes, ensure proper operator self-verifications, and drive proactive improvements through risk-based quality assurance methods.

The position reports to the Reliability & Mission Assurance team and serves as the quality assurance representative embedded in the subassembly production line. It plays a key role in maintaining product reliability, manufacturability, and compliance with space standards by implementing preventive quality practices, monitoring key metrics, and fostering a culture of quality ownership at the production level.

Who We Are


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

Your day-to-day responsibilities

  • Oversee subassembly production activities, ensuring compliance with quality requirements, approved processes, and product specifications.

  • Manage and support quality-related change management activities, including impact assessments, implementation follow-up, and effectiveness verification.

  • Review, approve, and disposition non-conformances, ensuring timely resolution through use-as-is, rework, repair, or corrective actions as appropriate.

  • Lead and support corrective and preventive action (CAPA) activities, including planning, implementation, and effectiveness monitoring.

  • Perform and oversee final inspection activities, including visual inspections, configuration verification, and confirmation of inspection and test results.

  • Prepare and review Acceptance Data Packages (ADPs) to ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance with customer and regulatory requirements.

  • Plan and conduct process audits, perform spot checks of newly implemented procedures, and follow up on corrective actions to verify sustained compliance.

  • Develop, maintain, and continuously improve inspection plans, checklists, quality requirements, and inspection procedures in collaboration with Engineering and Production teams.

  • Monitor production and quality performance indicators, including non-conformance trends, yields, rework, and process effectiveness, to drive continuous improvement.

  • Provide guidance and training to production personnel on quality requirements, inspection standards, ESD/FOD control, cleanliness, and product handling practices.

  • Ensure production readiness by verifying that required inspections, verifications, approvals, and quality gates are completed before manufacturing activities proceed.

  • Collaborate with Engineering, Production, and Quality teams to identify risks, resolve quality issues, and improve manufacturing and inspection processes.

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electronics, Mechatronics, or Electrical Engineering.

  • Familiarity with electronics or PCBA and high-reliability electronics production environment.

  • Minimum 5 years of experience in production quality assurance, manufacturing engineering, or process reliability within electronics, aerospace, or high-reliability manufacturing.

  • Solid understanding of subassembly production processes (gluing, soldering, assembly, and testing), process control, ESD/FOD/cleanliness requirements, and space or electronics manufacturing standards.

  • Familiarity with standards such as IPC-A-610 Class 3, IPC/WHMA-A-620 Class 3, J-STD-001, and quality systems (ISO 9001 / AS9100)

Department: Global Manufacturing Organisation

Reports to: Head of MAITE Spain

Location: Valencia, Spain

Type of Contract: Permanent

Why this role matters:

As an AIT Engineer, Harness & Thermal, you play a vital role in ensuring the thermal and electrical integrity of ICEYE's satellite constellation. You will execute hands-on assembly, integration, and testing activities, from harness routing and MLI installation to structural alignment and mission-critical verification. Working across mechanical, electrical, and design teams, you will own technical issues on the production floor and contribute directly to the quality and reliability of spacecraft leaving Valencia ready for orbit.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

Your day-to-day responsibilities

  • Assemble, route, and secure complex satellite electrical harnesses, ensuring compliance with routing standards and EMI/EMC best practices for grounding and shielding

  • Conduct alignment, assembly, and verification of mechanical and thermal hardware across satellite production activities

  • Identify process issues and drive continuous improvement of thermal and harness production workflows, contributing to design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-testability (DFT) initiatives

  • Represent AIT Engineering across projects and disciplines on mechanical and thermal interface topics, ensuring alignment between production and design teams

  • Fundamental understanding of EMI/EMC principles and best practices for aerospace cabling and harness design

  • Systems engineering mindset, able to identify and resolve issues across mechanical, thermal, and electrical interfaces

  • Track record of enabling design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-testability (DFT) in a production environment

  • Strong English communication skills (written and spoken) for cross-functional collaboration

jobs.title: Satellite Systems, Software Verification Team Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role Highlights

  • Satellite Systems, Software Verification Team Lead

  • Location: Valencia, Spain

  • Department: Global Manufacturing Organisation

  • Reports to: Maite Manager

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Office

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

About the Role

We are looking for an Satellite Systems, Software Verification Team Lead to own the final verification of our satellites, the stage where an integrated spacecraft is proven to work.

Once a satellite has been integrated, your team takes over. You’ll lead satellite-level functional and end-to-end checkout, onboard software loading and validation, and RF testing in our anechoic chamber, with a team of 5 technicians across systems, software and RF.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll spend real time with your team at the satellite, troubleshooting, unblocking issues and improving how we test. ICEYE is scaling satellite production fast, so you’ll also build the processes, tools and KPIs that let verification keep pace without compromising quality.

We’re looking for a strong electronics engineer who is comfortable with software and enjoys leading people. Space experience is a plus, not a requirement. If you’ve led hands-on electronics testing in a demanding industry such as aerospace, defence, automotive or power electronics, we’ll help you learn the space-specific parts.

 

Who We Are


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

 

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

 

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

 

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

Your day-to-day responsibilities

Leading Satellite Verification

  • Own satellite-level verification after integration: functional and end-to-end system checkout

  • Prove that all onboard systems (power, avionics, software, RF) perform reliably in full configuration

  • Be hands-on: lead troubleshooting, isolate faults, unblock issues and keep momentum

Owning Software in Verification

  • Own onboard software loading, validation and checkout during production verification

  • Maintain and improve test scripts, test automation and software-supported verification flows

  • Work with AIT Engineering on software-related issues, telling software faults apart from hardware faults

Overseeing RF Testing

  • Make sure RF testing of the satellite in the anechoic chamber is planned, executed and reported to standard, working with the RF specialists in your team

  • Keep RF test benches and chamber setups maintained, calibrated and compliant

Quality, Traceability & Compliance

  • Plan, execute and report system-level functional tests and inspections

  • Maintain configuration control, build discipline and full traceability

  • Ensure compliance with applicable aerospace quality standards such as ECSS

  • Identify key non-conformances, escalate critical issues and drive resolution of the most impactful ones, supporting root cause analysis led by AIT Engineering

Building Scalable, Repeatable Processes

  • Develop work instructions, test procedures and checklists with AIT Engineering and Quality

  • Turn unclear inputs into clear, usable processes and reduce tribal knowledge

  • Increase throughput and reduce rework while protecting quality

Leading & Developing the Team

  • Lead, coach and grow a multidisciplinary team of engineers and technicians

  • Build a culture of ownership, accountability and pride in the product

  • Teach structured fault diagnosis and test best practices

Working Across Teams

  • Be the bridge between verification and engineering (systems, software, RF, AIT)

  • Collaborate with Quality, Planning, Supply Chain and the two other production teams (Integration/Mechanical & Thermal; Electronics)

  • Prepare verification for higher volumes; define and track KPIs

What We're Looking For

You don’t need to tick every box. If you have most of the must-haves and the role excites you, we’d like to hear from you.

Must-haves

  • A degree in electronics, telecommunications or electrical engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience

  • Hands-on experience testing, validating or verifying complex electronic systems, at unit or system level

  • Working software knowledge: scripting (ideally Python), loading and configuring software on hardware, version and configuration control

  • Experience leading or coordinating a technical team in a hands-on environment

  • Ability to read schematics, assembly drawings and test procedures

  • Clear communication with engineers, technicians and stakeholders, in fluent English

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience in space, aerospace, defence or another high-reliability industry

  • RF test experience (spectrum or network analysers, signal generators, anechoic chambers)

  • Familiarity with ECSS, NASA-STD or similar standards (such as DO-178C, ISO 26262 or EN 50128)

  • Test automation frameworks (such as TestStand, LabVIEW or pytest)

  • Experience scaling a test or production process

 

What Success Looks Like

  • Every satellite is verified reliably, predictably, and to standard before it ships

  • RF, system, and software verification processes are clear, structured, and scalable

  • Problems are isolated and solved at the root, not patched

  • The team takes full ownership of verification quality and traceability

  • Verification keeps pace with ICEYE's growth

 

Why This Role Is Interesting

  • You own the moment of truth, proving the satellite works end-to-end

  • You'll bring RF, systems, and software verification together under one scope

  • You'll shape how verification is done, not just follow existing processes

  • You'll work at the intersection of engineering and production, where decisions have immediate impact

Application Process

  • Talent Acquisition Interview

  • Hiring Manager General Interview

  • Technical Interview, including a Technical Challenge

  • Peer & Culture Interview

  • VP Interview

  • Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

 - Build a culture of ownership, accountability and pride in the product

 - Teach structured fault diagnosis and test best practices

 - Experience leading or coordinating a technical team in a hands-on environment

 - Ability to read schematics, assembly drawings and test procedures

 - Clear communication with engineers, technicians and stakeholders, in fluent English

  • Department: Global Manufacturing Organisation

As a Systems and Software Verification Engineer, you play a vital role in bringing every satellite that reaches our Valencia production line to operational readiness. You will own the first power-on, initial software and firmware loading, and end-to-end systems verification of fully integrated SAR satellites, running automated functional, power, and bus test campaigns, diagnosing issues at the boundary between software, firmware, and electronics hardware, and ensuring configuration control on final activities. Your work lets test campaigns run independently on the line, without pulling engineers away from other teams.

Who We Are
ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

Your day-to-day responsibilities

  • Execute initial satellite power-on, firmware flashing, and subsystem communication verifications.

  • Run, debug, and execute automated functional, power, and bus test scripts using Python, Shell, and Linux environments.

  • Work with Git repositories to manage test code, track updates, and verify software builds.

  • Operate mechanical and electrical ground support equipment (GSE), and troubleshoot electronic hardware, power distribution, and digital interface issues using lab instruments (oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters).

  • Diagnose whether an anomaly is a test setup issue or a genuine unit fault, and raise non-conformance reports (NCRs) in Jira.

  • Maintain detailed test logs and accurate documentation, and ensure configuration control on final activities.

  • Assist in managing activities related to satellite launch campaigns.

  • Actively contribute to continuous improvement initiatives - procedures, processes, tools, test automation, and 6S.

  • Assist in training and mentoring junior technicians, and communicate proactively with team members and supervisors regarding any challenges or obstacles.

  • Work closely with the RF Senior Technician, AIT Engineering, and Quality, ensuring clear communication so that satellite build-phase deadlines and technical specifications are met.

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

  • Relevant university degree in Aeronautical Engineering, Space Studies, Applied Physics, Electronics, or similar, or equivalent hands-on experience in a related role.

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience setting up, debugging, and running real test benches and satellite systems or interfaces, not just executing someone else’s scripts.

  • Proficient in a Linux environment, comfortable modifying and debugging Python scripts, and working with Git.

  • Systems thinking across avionics, power, and software, enough to tell a test setup fault from a genuine unit fault.

  • Experience using lab equipment such as power supplies, multimeters, and oscilloscopes.

  • Excellent communication skills, with particular attention to detail in procedures, preparation, and execution.

  • Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, assembly instructions, and schematics.

  • Proficient in English, both written and spoken, to ensure clear communication in a cross-functional environment.

Nice to haves:

  • ICEYE-specific test frameworks, satellite bus specifics, Jira and MES flow, and launch campaign procedures.

  • Space or satellite AIT (Assembly, Integration, and Testing) background.

  • Experience with environmental testing (e.g. vibration/shaker rigs, thermal testing).

  • Experience using Atlassian Cloud (Jira, Confluence).

  • Lean & Six Sigma experience.

  • Hiring Manager General Interview

  • Technical Interview, including a Technical Challenge

  • Final Interview

  • Location: Espoo, Finland

  • Department: Manufacturing Assurance; Global Manufacturing Organisation

  • Reports to: Configuration and Change Team Lead

This role is vital for maintaining the day-to-day operational integrity of our product data as we scale across multi-domain environments for multi-site manufacturing..

As a Configuration Specialist, your mission is to ensure that product information is accurately entered, tracked, and maintained within our systems. Reporting to the CM Team Leader, you will support GMO and the engineering teams by administering change documentation, routing approvals, and ensuring adherence to configuration standards.

  • Support the implementation of the Configuration Management Standard Operating Procedures (CM SOPs) by executing daily CM administrative tasks and ensuring process compliance.

  • Perform data entry and maintain accurate product baselines within PLM and MES systems under the guidance of the team.

  • Drive and administer the change management workflows; route ECRs, ECOs, Deviations, and Waivers for approval, track their status, and prepare agendas/minutes for reviewers/approvers.

  • Ensure that new parts and documents strictly adhere to established item classification schemes and part numbering conventions.

  • Generate regular configuration status reports and extract CM metrics to support the team’s KPI tracking.

  • Maintain organized configuration records and ensure all documentation is properly archived and accessible for audits.

  • Understanding of the distinction between EBOM and MBOM, product breakdown structures, and item classification methodologies.

  • Ability to communicate technical and process-related information clearly across diverse teams, including Engineering, Manufacturing, and Operations, and to support alignment in a cross-functional environment.

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with changing priorities.

  • Fluent in English.

Nice to haves:

  • Exposure to the aerospace, defense, or automotive manufacturing industries.

  • Basic awareness of configuration management standards (e.g., ECSS-M-ST-40, EIA-649) or willingness to learn.

  • Familiarity with software version control tools (e.g., Git, Jira) or software development lifecycles.

  • Experience in drafting technical documentation or standard operating procedures (SOPs).

  • Experience in a manufacturing scale-up or transition environment.

jobs.title: Supplier Quality Engineer (Mechanical)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role highlights:

  • Location: Finland

  • Department: Reliability & Mission Assurance

  • Reports to: Manager, Reliability & Mission Assurance

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Office

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

Why this role matters:

This role is responsible for ensuring the quality, maturity, and continuous improvement of ICEYE’s supplier base, from selection through ongoing performance management. The Supplier Quality Engineer leads supplier preselection and audits, manages technical and quality requirement flow-down, drives supplier change control and supplier part qualification activities to ensure reliable, compliant, and manufacturable products.

The position reports to the Mission Assurance & Reliability team and collaborates closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, and AIT Engineering. It plays a key role in strengthening ICEYE’s supply ecosystem by aligning supplier capabilities with design and production needs, enabling scalable and reliable manufacturing operations across all external partners.

Who We Are


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.


Your day-to-day responsibilities

 

  • Lead supplier preselection and follow-up audits to assess capability, maturity, and compliance with ICEYE and industry standards.

  • Define and communicate technical and quality requirements to suppliers, ensuring full understanding and compliance throughout the supply chain.

  • Monitor supplier performance using defined metrics (e.g., delivery quality, NCR rates, on-time delivery, responsiveness) to identify gaps and drive improvement actions.

  • Manage supplier change requests, part and process approvals, and configuration control activities in coordination with the Engineering Teams and Configuration Management Team.

  • Lead supplier part qualification activities ensuring compliance with technical, quality, and regulatory requirements prior to production release.

  • Identify, assess, and proactively mitigate supplier-related risks, ensuring continuity of supply and minimizing impact to product quality and delivery.

  • Collaborate early with Design and AIT Engineering teams to gather manufacturability and inspectability feedback from suppliers.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
• Senior Electronics Engineer

  • Department: Engineering

  • Location: Warsaw, Poland

  • Reports to: Engineering Lead, AOCS Hardware

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Office

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO)

 

The Mission of the Senior Electronics Engineer

You ensure that our AOCS system delivers reliable and consistent performance through innovative power electronics design and precision control systems. Beyond this, you will also have the opportunity to design other high-speed, high-power, and high-reliability electronics supporting ICEYE's growing constellation of diverse spacecraft.

This role is within the Attitude and Orbit Control domain where we are responsible for developing and maintaining the power electronics and control systems that enable our AOCS capabilities.

Your job will be to work closely with production teams, operations teams, and software teams to ensure smooth and performant operation of our propulsion systems in development and deployed environments. Expect to be involved in the complete lifecycle of the system - from design phases of next-generation propulsion architectures to maintenance and optimization of existing systems we and our customers operate.

We move fast. At ICEYE, you are expected to understand the whole system - not just your slice of it - and to iterate quickly. Designs you work on today can be launching to orbit within months, not years. This is an environment where your decisions carry real weight and your work becomes tangible faster than almost anywhere else in the industry.

You will have a direct impact on mission success as the performance and reliability of our AOCS electronics directly affect the operational capabilities we deliver to our customers and the overall performance of our fleet.

Who We Are


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

 
 

Your day-to-day responsibilities:

  • Own the full design lifecycle of flight hardware - from first schematics and component selection through bring-up, functional and environmental testing, launch, and on-orbit operations - creating a tight learning and improvement loop at every stage

  • Develop a deep understanding of the complete AOCS system, including the interplay between power electronics, control systems, and the spacecraft subsystems they drive

  • Lead the design of power electronics and control electronics for AOCS hardware, including power conversion, distribution, and precision control circuits

  • Design and optimize power electronics for efficiency, thermal management, and performance across all operational environments

  • Develop precision analog and data acquisition circuits for power measurement, voltage/current monitoring, signal conditioning, and feedback control

  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues across the full lifecycle - design, prototyping, manufacturing, field operation, and on-orbit anomalies

  • Work closely with firmware engineers, FPGA engineers, software developers, and mechanical and thermal engineers to ensure seamless integration

  • Mentor junior engineers to continuously raise the bar on design and testing practices

What we’re looking for:


Must haves:

  • MSc in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or related field with 5+ years of professional experience in high-voltage electronics

  • Proven expertise in high-voltage electronics (250V+) design, high-voltage topologies, switching architectures, power management, and low-noise power supply design

  • Advanced analog circuit design: precision measurement, sensor interface and signal conditioning, low-noise amplifier design, and transimpedance circuits

  • Advanced proficiency with circuit simulation and PCB design tools like, LTSpice and Altium.

  • Understanding of high-speed signal design: signal integrity, timing analysis, and EMI/EMC principles for noise mitigation in high-voltage switching environments

  • Experience designing embedded control hardware for power electronics: microcontroller interfaces (ADC, PWM, GPIO), protection circuits (overcurrent/overvoltage detection), fault handling, and safe-state transitions

  • Experience designing serial communication hardware (RS485, UART) with proper isolation, impedance matching, and protection

  • Ability to work closely with firmware engineers to define hardware interfaces, protection circuits, telemetry acquisition and develop joint verification test cases

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams

Nice to haves:

  • Hands-on experience with environmental testing (vibration, thermal, radiation, vacuum) and harsh operating conditions

  • Fundamental understanding of control systems, feedback loops, and closed-loop circuit design

  • Experience designing solenoid valve driver circuits for high-current on/off switching, including flyback protection and inductive load management

  • Experience with wide-bandgap semiconductor technologies (GaN, SiC MOSFETs)

  • Experience with design for manufacturability (DFM) and cost optimization

  • Proficiency in programming languages (C, Python) for firmware integration or hardware characterization

 
 

Application process

  • Talent Acquisition Interview

  • Hiring Manager Interview

  • Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge

  • Hiring Team Interview

  • Offer Decision

Working at ICEYE

At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.

How We Work (Our Values)

Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.

  • Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.

  • See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.

  • Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

  • Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

  • Have fun: What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing—at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.

Our commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We want ICEYE to be a place where people can be themselves and do great work. Different backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, which is why we work to create an environment where people feel included, respected, and able to speak up. Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table.

We’re committed to fair, inclusive hiring and equal opportunity. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, tell us—we’ll do our best to help.

Apply now to start your ICEYE journey, and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at iceye.com

  • Contribute to and improve AIT documentation including RF test procedures, integration plans, and configuration records

  • Proficient English (written and spoken) for cross-functional collaboration

  • Track record of enabling design-for-testability (DFT) and design-for-manufacturing (DFM)

  • Lean and Six Sigma experience

  • Experience with SAR payload calibration or comms link-budget analysis beyond routine test execution

  • Experience writing or improving Python test scripts beyond routine execution

  • Proficient Japanese (written and spoken)
