jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role highlights:

  • Senior Fullstack Engineer

  • Location: Espoo

  • Department: Engineering, Fleet Control and Communications

  • Reports to: Engineering Manager, Fleet UI

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Hybrid

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

Why this role matters:

As a Senior Fullstack Engineer in Fleet UI team you will be building a mission-critical system used by satellite operators. The problems are technically rich: managing satellite configurations, visualizing orbits in 3D, managing passes across a global network of ground stations, automating mission operations and more. You will work in a domain where the UI decisions directly impact satellite mission outcomes.

Who We Are

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE’s world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world’s largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy – day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE’s near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring (including oil-spill detection), and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.

ICEYE is headquartered in Finland and operates globally across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We have more than 900 employees, united by a shared vision: improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.

 



Your day-to-day responsibilities

 

  • Build, and maintain features across a React + TypeScript project serving real-time satellite operations

  • Collaborate closely with a UI/UX designer in developing sophisticated UI components and data visualizations tools including timeline views, 3D globe rendering (Cesium), and pass planning interfaces

  • Contribute occasionally to backend APIs (Node, Python) to unblock delivery when needed

  • Drive frontend architecture decisions — state management strategy, component design, performance optimization

  • Support the team with DevOps work across multiple environments — including managing Docker-based deployments, configuring environment-specific runtime settings, and contributing to release workflows

  • Write and maintain unit tests (Jest + Testing Library) and end-to-end tests (Playwright)

  • Participate in code reviews, uphold coding standards, and mentor engineers on best practices

  • Contribute to CI/CD pipelines and oversee migration from Webpack 5 to Vite

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

  • 5+ years of professional experience building fullstack production-grade applications using React, TypeScript (ES6+) and Node

  • Experience writing clean, maintainable code in Python

  • Strong understanding of component-based architecture, modern React patterns, and state management approaches

  • Experience designing, developing, and consuming RESTful and GraphQL APIs

  • Solid testing discipline, including unit and end-to-end testing with tools such as Jest and Playwright

  • Experience with modern frontend tooling and build systems such as Vite, webpack, and npm

  • Proficiency with Git and collaborative development workflows
    Active use of AI-assisted development tools

  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to debug complex, cross-layer issues

  • Understanding of web application security best practices

  • Relevant higher education degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field


Nice to haves

  • Solid understanding of API design, including REST principles and GraphQL schema design

  • Knowledge of database design and ORM frameworks

  • Experience with modern DevOps practices including CI/CD pipelines, containerization, and cloud platforms such as AWS

  • Familiarity with infrastructure and deployment tooling such as Kubernetes, Terraform, Helm, or ArgoCD


Application Process

  • Talent Partner Screen Call

  • Hiring Manager Interview

  • Technical Interview

  • Values & Fit Interview

jobs.title: AIT Engineering Team Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role Highlights:

  • Title: AIT Engineering Team Lead

  • Department: Global Manufacturing Organization

  • Reports to: Head of MAITE, Optics

  • Location: Warsaw, Poland

  • Type of Contract: Permanent

  • Working model: On-site

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

Why this role matters:

ICEYE is seeking a Team Lead, AIT Engineering to lead the AIT Engineering function responsible for the assembly, integration, and testing of satellite systems and optical payloads.

This is a technical leadership and people management role in an early-stage production environment, where products, processes, and manufacturing capabilities are continuously evolving. You will lead and develop the AIT Engineering team while acting as the technical focal point for AIT activities during spacecraft builds and integration campaigns.

The role sits at the interface between Engineering and Production. You will work closely with optical, mechanical, electrical, systems, quality, and production teams to translate design intent into robust, manufacturable, integrable, and testable processes, while ensuring that feedback and issues identified during production are effectively driven back into Engineering.

You will also support the integration and validation of externally supplied optical payloads, working with internal engineering teams and external suppliers to ensure successful integration into the satellite platform.

The role requires a strong background in spacecraft AIT, system integration, or complex hardware integration, combined with the ability to lead people, coordinate technical activities, develop robust processes, and drive execution in a fast-paced production environment.

Who We Are
ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

What you will do

  • Lead and develop the AIT Engineering team, providing technical direction, mentoring, and clear priorities.

  • Lead the assembly, integration, and testing of spacecraft systems, acting as the technical focal point during spacecraft builds.

  • Support the integration and validation of externally supplied optical payloads into the spacecraft platform.

  • Combine technical leadership with hands-on involvement in spacecraft integration, testing, troubleshooting, and verification.

  • Ensure AIT readiness before builds, including tools, GSE, procedures, documentation, hardware, and engineering support.

  • Drive structured problem-solving and root cause analysis of integration and test issues, ensuring lessons learned are fed back into Engineering and production.

  • Act as the bridge between Production and Engineering, translating design requirements into practical, manufacturable, and testable integration processes.

  • Work closely with Systems, Mechanical, Electrical, Optical, Quality, Manufacturing, and external suppliers to resolve integration challenges.

  • Define and continuously improve AIT processes, procedures, test methods, tooling, fixtures, and technical documentation.

  • Support production ramp-up by improving integration efficiency, repeatability, reliability, and scalability.

  • Mentor engineers and build strong technical capabilities within the AIT organization.

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in spacecraft AIT, system integration, testing, or production of complex hardware systems.

  • Strong experience with spacecraft integration and system-level testing across multiple engineering disciplines.

  • Experience with optical systems, optomechanics, optical payloads, or Earth Observation systems.

  • Experience working with complex precision hardware in cleanroom or controlled environments.

  • Strong system-level understanding across mechanical, electrical, optical, and systems engineering.

  • Experience with DFM / DFT principles and translating design requirements into manufacturable and testable solutions.

  • Experience with AIT processes, test procedures, verification, and technical documentation.

  • Experience with GSE, tooling, fixtures, or test setups used for integration and testing.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills, including structured root cause analysis and corrective actions.

  • Experience working with MES, ERP, test data management, or similar production systems.

  • Experience with Lean manufacturing or continuous improvement methodologies.

  • Strong understanding of configuration-controlled production and engineering environments.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

  • Strong written and spoken English.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience with optical alignment and metrology, including focus, tilt, centering, boresight, interferometry, collimators, or MTF.

  • Experience supporting environmental testing, such as thermal vacuum, vibration, or EMC.

  • Experience working with external suppliers or partners, particularly payload suppliers.

  • Experience supporting products from prototype through production ramp-up.

  • Experience with PDR, CDR, PRR, or equivalent technical and production readiness reviews.

  • Experience with PFMEA, process capability, or other manufacturing engineering tools.

  • Experience in Lean manufacturing, industrialization, or production scale-up.

Application Process

  • Talent Acquisition interview

  • Hiring manager interview

  • Technical interview, including a technical challenge

Your work will go beyond dashboards and alerts. You’ll reduce operational noise, eliminate blind spots, and give product teams the tools and autonomy to run reliable services.

Your day-to-day responsibilities

  • Own and continuously improve a unified, production-grade observability stack covering metrics, logs, and traces, giving every team a consistent, self-service way to understand and operate the health of their services.

  • Build and maintain trusted alerting by tuning alerts against clear SLOs/SLIs, reducing noise, improving ownership and ensuring real issues surface early.

  • Define, document, and drive adoption of instrumentation standards covering metric naming, label cardinality, structured logging, and distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry.

  • Enable product teams to diagnose and resolve incidents faster through well-designed dashboards, runbooks, hands-on support, and practical observability guidance.

  • Run the observability platform like a product, owning its roadmap, interfaces, reliability, scalability, and cost across areas such as retention, sampling, and cardinality.

  • Provide clear technical direction for observability across the engineering organisation, making pragmatic architectural trade-offs and helping teams adopt platform capabilities effectively.

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

1. Observability platform ownership at scale

6+ years in Platform Engineering, Observability, or infrastructure roles, with end-to-end ownership of a production observability stack (for example the LGTM stack - Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir/Prometheus - or an equivalent metrics/logs/traces platform) at scale.

  • Instrumentation & telemetry: OpenTelemetry adoption, metric and label design, structured logging, and distributed tracing across complex, multi-team systems.

  • SLO/SLI & error budgets: dashboards and alerting that surface real problems early while minimizing noise and false positives.

  • Platform as a product: treating other engineering teams as customers, with clear interfaces and a roadmap shaped by their needs.

  • Alerting & reliability attitude: comfortable with on-call, driving blameless learning from incidents, and continuously tuning signal quality instead of letting alert fatigue set in.

2. Software engineering foundation

  • A background that includes time spent writing and shipping production software, bringing engineering instincts to building tooling and automation rather than only operating what already exists.

  • Proficiency in at least one backend language (for example Python or Go) for automation, tooling, and building internal observability capabilities.

3. Long-term ownership of your own decisions

Demonstrated experience owning the long-term consequences of your own architectural and tooling decisions - having lived with what you built through its maintenance, upgrades, and failure modes, not just its initial rollout.

4. Communication

Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, able to explain complex system behavior clearly to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to haves:

1. Platform & telemetry breadth

  • Rancher, Istio, and Kubernetes-native observability patterns (service mesh telemetry, sidecars, eBPF-based tooling).

  • Bridging hybrid environments across AWS and on-prem platforms such as vSphere/VxRail.

  • Managing cost and cardinality on large-scale telemetry pipelines (retention policies, sampling, downsampling).

2. Practices that spread beyond your own team

  • Defining SLO/SLI frameworks or observability standards adopted across multiple teams.

  • Running or contributing to incident response and blameless postmortem processes.

  • Mentoring engineers and raising engineering maturity through technical leadership and enablement.

Background in regulated, security-sensitive, or mission-critical domains.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role highlights:

  • Staff/Lead Product Designer, Design System

  • Location: Espoo, Uusimaa, Finland

  • Department: Product Management

  • Reports to: Director of Product Design

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Hybrid (3 days / week in office)

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)


Why this role matters:

We don't have a design system. What we have is a set of products built fast, for users who needed the imagery yesterday, that share a brand without sharing much else. Buttons that quietly disagree with each other. Spacing as a matter of personal taste. Several defensible ways to build a table, none of them the same. Nobody was sloppy - this is what shipping under real pressure leaves behind, and the interest on it now comes out of every sprint.

As a Staff / Lead Product Designer, you'll build the thing from nothing. That starts small and slightly unglamorous: a Figma library people actually reach for and a design playbook that settles the arguments worth settling. Then tokens with a structure that holds. Then components in code, documented well enough that nobody has to ask you how they work. By the time it's a design system in the full sense, the hardest part - people using it by default - is already solved, because you'll have built it in the open with the teams who had to adopt it.

This is a hands-on, opinionated, sleeves-rolled-up role. You'll be the highest craft bar in the domain and the person who raises everyone else's. You'll spend as much time with frontend engineers as with designers, quite possibly in their repo.

Real ownership. Very little existing process to inherit. If that sounds like a warning, it isn't. It's the job.


Who We Are

ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific..


Your day-to-day responsibilities

  • Start with a library and a playbook. Grow it into a system. Early on that means a Figma library, shared foundations and written guidance that gives teams a default instead of a decision. Later it means token architecture, components in code and documentation that scales past you. You'll decide the sequence, what's a token and what's a local decision, and where the line sits between flexibility and consistency. Those calls are yours to make, not to wait for.

  • Co-design with frontend, in the code. Our engineers will build most of the components. You'll be in the conversation about props, state and composition, reading PRs and prototyping in a branch when that's the fastest way to prove a point. Figma is where you think, not where the system ends up living.

  • Sell it. Repeatedly. A design system nobody adopts is a very tidy failure. You'll make the case to product managers, engineers and leadership, run office hours, and do migration work yourself when that's what unblocks a team.

  • Set and hold the craft bar. Across the whole domain, at the pixel level, in public. Kind about people, uncompromising about the work.

  • Put AI to actual work. Component documentation, variant generation, token maintenance, migration codemods, spec drafting. The tedious 60% of systems work is exactly what these tools are good at, and we want someone with strong instincts about which 60%.

  • Stay accountable for what ships. Adoption, consistency, shipped UI quality, how quickly teams can build - not the size of your Figma library.

  • Work across a big, networked organisation. Designers in other domains, brand and marketing design, sales engineers, customers. Consistency is a negotiation, not a mandate you email out.


What we're looking for

Must haves:

  • You've done 0-to-1 before, somewhere messy. You've taken a design system from nothing to adopted, in an organisation that had neither and wasn't yet convinced it needed one. You know how the first six months actually go, which corners are safe to cut, and how to structure tokens so they survive the next product rather than getting quietly forked.

  • You're fluent enough in code to be useful. Reading React and CSS, understanding component APIs, running the repo locally, opening a PR without ceremony. You don't need to be an engineer, but you do need to hold your end of a technical conversation and design things that are buildable as drawn.

  • You can influence without authority. You'll spend real energy convincing people who have their own roadmaps and their own deadlines. Being right won't be enough and you know that already.

  • Your craft is exceptional. Deep command of layout systems, typography, colour and visual hierarchy, applied in dense, complex professional interfaces. Detail-obsessed in the good way: the way that makes a whole product feel considered.

  • You have a real point of view on AI in design work. Not a vibe, a practice. You've used these tools to accelerate documentation, generate and audit variants, maintain tokens, or migrate code, and you can tell us where they helped and where they made a confident mess.

  • You've owned UX end-to-end for complex professional products. Discovery through shipped product through what you learned afterwards, with a portfolio that shows the systems thinking as well as the surfaces. Expert in Figma.


Nice to haves:

  • Accessibility as a default rather than an audit.

  • Experience with theming, dark mode, or multi-brand systems.

  • Data-dense, map-heavy or real-time interfaces.

  • Public writing or open-source contribution on design systems.

  • Time spent in high-stakes or regulated environments where getting it wrong is expensive.

The disposition, which matters more than any of the above: outcome-driven thinking over perfect artifacts (design is what ships); curiosity about users, about design and technology trends and history, and about better ways of working; pragmatic product judgment, knowing when "good and shipped" beats "perfect but late"; clear communication and respectful collaboration.

  1. Recruiter screen

  2. Hiring Manager interview

  3. Portfolio review

  4. Task

  5. Final interview

That starts small and slightly unglamorous: a Figma library people actually reach for and a design playbook that settles the arguments worth settling. Then tokens with a structure that holds. Then components in code, documented well enough that nobody has to ask you how they work. By the time it's a design system in the full sense, the hardest part - people using it by default - is already solved, because you'll have built it in the open with the teams who had to adopt it.

This is a hands-on, opinionated, sleeves-rolled-up role. You'll be the highest craft bar in the domain and the person who raises everyone else's. You'll spend as much time with frontend engineers as with designers, quite possibly in their repo. 

Real ownership. Very little existing process to inherit. If that sounds like a warning, it isn't. It's the job.




WHO WE ARE

ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system. ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future. Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific..



YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Start with a library and a playbook. Grow it into a system. Early on that means a Figma library, shared foundations and written guidance that gives teams a default instead of a decision. Later it means token architecture, components in code and documentation that scales past you. You'll decide the sequence, what's a token and what's a local decision, and where the line sits between flexibility and consistency. Those calls are yours to make, not to wait for.

 - Co-design with frontend, in the code. Our engineers will build most of the components. You'll be in the conversation about props, state and composition, reading PRs and prototyping in a branch when that's the fastest way to prove a point. Figma is where you think, not where the system ends up living.

 - Sell it. Repeatedly. A design system nobody adopts is a very tidy failure. You'll make the case to product managers, engineers and leadership, run office hours, and do migration work yourself when that's what unblocks a team.

 - Set and hold the craft bar. Across the whole domain, at the pixel level, in public. Kind about people, uncompromising about the work.

 - Put AI to actual work. Component documentation, variant generation, token maintenance, migration codemods, spec drafting. The tedious 60% of systems work is exactly what these tools are good at, and we want someone with strong instincts about which 60%.

 - Stay accountable for what ships. Adoption, consistency, shipped UI quality, how quickly teams can build - not the size of your Figma library.

 - Work across a big, networked organisation. Designers in other domains, brand and marketing design, sales engineers, customers. Consistency is a negotiation, not a mandate you email out.
   



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Must haves:

 - You've done 0-to-1 before, somewhere messy. You've taken a design system from nothing to adopted, in an organisation that had neither and wasn't yet convinced it needed one. You know how the first six months actually go, which corners are safe to cut, and how to structure tokens so they survive the next product rather than getting quietly forked.

 - You're fluent enough in code to be useful. Reading React and CSS, understanding component APIs, running the repo locally, opening a PR without ceremony. You don't need to be an engineer, but you do need to hold your end of a technical conversation and design things that are buildable as drawn.

 - You can influence without authority. You'll spend real energy convincing people who have their own roadmaps and their own deadlines. Being right won't be enough and you know that already.

 - Your craft is exceptional. Deep command of layout systems, typography, colour and visual hierarchy, applied in dense, complex professional interfaces. Detail-obsessed in the good way: the way that makes a whole product feel considered.

 - You have a real point of view on AI in design work. Not a vibe, a practice. You've used these tools to accelerate documentation, generate and audit variants, maintain tokens, or migrate code, and you can tell us where they helped and where they made a confident mess.

 - You've owned UX end-to-end for complex professional products. Discovery through shipped product through what you learned afterwards, with a portfolio that shows the systems thinking as well as the surfaces. Expert in Figma.



NICE TO HAVES:

 - Accessibility as a default rather than an audit.

 - Experience with theming, dark mode, or multi-brand systems.

 - Data-dense, map-heavy or real-time interfaces.

 - Public writing or open-source contribution on design systems.

 - Time spent in high-stakes or regulated environments where getting it wrong is expensive.

The disposition, which matters more than any of the above: outcome-driven thinking over perfect artifacts (design is what ships); curiosity about users, about design and technology trends and history, and about better ways of working; pragmatic product judgment, knowing when "good and shipped" beats "perfect but late"; clear communication and respectful collaboration.




APPLICATION PROCESS

 1. Recruiter screen

 2. Hiring Manager interview

 3. Portfolio review

 4. Task

 5. Final interview

At ICEYE, you'll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role highlights:

  • Flight Software Deployment Engineer

  • Location: Warsaw, Poland/ Espoo, Finland

  • Department: Flight Software Build & Release Team

  • Reports to: Flight Software Build & Release Team Lead

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Hybrid (3 days in the office)

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

Why this role matters:

The Build & Release team owns the path from source to flight-ready software across growing satellite constellations. This role exists because every artifact that reaches satellites in orbit must be reproducible, traceable, and verifiable. A bad update is not a simple rollback, it could mean a satellite becomes at risk.

This is not a generic SRE or DevOps role, the production environment is composed of satellites flying 500 km above our heads, and the software artifacts are cross-compiled embedded binaries. The role is in the realm of half build engineering and half embedded Linux development, you need to be willing to work at both ends.

Satellites are treated to OTA updates regularly which our team must make sure are built and deployed the right way, utilizing software development best practices.

Who We Are


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.


Your day-to-day responsibilities

 

  • Hands on software engineering of our satellite on-board updating system, built to deploy software and firmware updates: features, maintenance, tests and documentation.

  • Contribute to the build layer across the flight software domain, so every repository is built, versioned and packaged the same way.

  • Enforce immutable releases and harden the packaging and signing pipelines: least-privilege permissions, pinned workflows and dependencies, approvals, and proper signing key management.

  • Work with the Linux platform team on how updates land on the satellite on-board computers, covering packaging format, filesystem layout and access control, making sure what we build installs cleanly and safely.


What we’re looking for

Must haves:

  • Embedded software engineering experience, with hands-on embedded Linux development: cross-compilation for ARM or similar targets, kernel configuration, device tree overlays, root filesystem and image construction.

  • Production CI/CD experience for compiled artifacts, not only containers or web deployments. GitHub Actions specifically is required, and workflow hardening experience is valuable.

  • Working proficiency in C and C++ build environments, and in Python and Bash for automation.

  • Experience implementing release integrity controls, immutable artifacts storage. Signing key management, PKI and trust chains, AWS object-lock storage and cloud key management are all valuable here.

  • Shipping software to embedded devices already in the field with a package-based update mechanism, ideally opkg, under controlled release processes, quality gates and formal sign-of

Nice to haves:

  • Command of CMake, including multi-repository setups, toolchain files, and shared build infrastructure that other teams consume. Buildroot experience is relevant here.

Application Process

  • Conversation with talent acquisition (~30 min).

  • Screening with the hiring manager (~60 min).

  • Technical test - take home task to be completed in 3 to 5 working days.

  • Technical deep-dive (~90 min).

  • On-site office visit & director interview (~60 min).

Working at ICEYE

At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.

  • Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.

  • See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.

  • Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

  • Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

  • Have fun: What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing, at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

jobs.title: Senior Production Technician (Mechanical & Thermal)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role highlights:

  • Location: Espoo, Finland

  • Department: Production Finland

  • Reports to: Satellite Production Team Leader

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Onsite

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

Why this role matters:

We are looking for a Senior Mechanical & Thermal Production Technician to strengthen our satellite production operations as we scale toward standardized, repeatable, high-volume manufacturing.

In this hands-on role, you will independently execute complex assembly, subsystem integration, and thermal verification testing following detailed work instructions and AIT procedures. You will act as a technical anchor for your assigned production area, ensuring workstation readiness and driving frontline troubleshooting alongside Specialists and AIT Engineering.

We seek a proactive technical expert who takes full ownership of build activities, models high standards of quality and ESD compliance, and coaches technicians to elevate team capabilities and process stability.

Who We Are


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.


Your day-to-day responsibilities

 

  • Perform and support mechanical assembly, integration, and testing of precision, high-value hardware.

  • Take ownership of day-to-day technical readiness in your assigned production area, including tools, fixtures, work instructions, and workstation setup.

  • Provide practical guidance, troubleshooting support, and on-the-job coaching to technicians, helping them build confidence and independence.

  • Collaborate with Senior Technician, Production Line Owners, and AIT Engineering to investigate root causes and implement corrective actions for build issues and non-conformances (NCs).

  • Verify your work through continuity, insulation resistance, pin retention, and visual inspection against defined acceptance criteria

  • Build to IPC/WHMA-A-620 workmanship standards, with training and certification provided

  • Strictly follow work instructions, travelers, and checklists, completing all documentation accurately and in real time

  • Identify and report build or process deviations immediately, raising NCRs and supporting root cause analysis with accurate technical observations

  • Kit, label, and identify parts correctly, maintaining full traceability throughout the build

  • Carry out general electronics lab tasks as needed

  • Maintain a clean, organised, and audit-ready work environment compliant with ESD, safety, and cleanliness standards

  • 1-2 years of practical experience in cable and harness assembly, electromechanical assembly, or electronic assembly and test

  • Excellent manual dexterity and comfort working with small components, fine wires, and connectors

  • Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, wire tables, schematics, and wiring diagrams

  • Strong attention to detail and a proven ability to follow strict technical procedures and documentation requirements

  • Proficient English (written and spoken) for cross-functional collaboration

  • IPC certifications, particularly IPC/WHMA-A-620 or IPC J-STD-001 (Space Addendum)

  • Experience with coaxial, shielded, or high-speed cable assemblies

  • Broader electronics assembly experience such as PCB handling, conformal coating, or rework

  • Previous work in a cleanroom or under formal ESD controls

  • Familiarity with aerospace standards (ECSS, IPC) and configuration control

  • Experience with Atlassian Cloud tools (Jira, Confluence)

  • Spanish language skills for day-to-day collaboration on the production floor

  • Aerospace or space industry background

  • Lean and Six Sigma experience

As a Production Technician, Harness, you build the electrical backbone of ICEYE's satellites. Every subsystem on the spacecraft, from power to command and data handling, depends on harnesses being manufactured, routed, and verified correctly. You will execute assigned harness manufacturing, installation, and verification tasks with high precision, following established procedures and work instructions. Working under the guidance of Senior Technicians and Production Line Owners, you are responsible for the quality of your individual work and for making sure every harness leaving Valencia is ready to fly.



Who We Are:

ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

 - Install, route, and secure harnesses onto satellite assemblies alongside the integration team, respecting bend radii, strain relief, and routing standards

 - Verify your work through continuity, insulation resistance, pin retention, and visual inspection against defined acceptance criteria

 - Build to IPC/WHMA-A-620 workmanship standards, with training and certification provided

 - Strictly follow work instructions, travelers, and checklists, completing all documentation accurately and in real time

 - Identify and report build or process deviations immediately, raising NCRs and supporting root cause analysis with accurate technical observations

 - Kit, label, and identify parts correctly, maintaining full traceability throughout the build

 - Carry out general electronics lab tasks as needed

 - Maintain a clean, organised, and audit-ready work environment compliant with ESD, safety, and cleanliness standards

 - 1-2 years of practical experience in cable and harness assembly, electromechanical assembly, or electronic assembly and test

 - Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, wire tables, schematics, and wiring diagrams

 - Strong attention to detail and a proven ability to follow strict technical procedures and documentation requirements

 - Proficient English (written and spoken) for cross-functional collaboration

 - Experience with coaxial, shielded, or high-speed cable assemblies

 - Broader electronics assembly experience such as PCB handling, conformal coating, or rework

 - Previous work in a cleanroom or under formal ESD controls

 - Familiarity with aerospace standards (ECSS, IPC) and configuration control

 - Spanish language skills for day-to-day collaboration on the production floor

  • Perform handling and lifting operations with MGSE, including satellite rotation, transfer between stands and installation on test adapters.

  • Route, install and connect flight harnesses, including crimping, soldering, shielding, connector mating and identification.

  • Practical skill in precision mechanical assembly and thermal hardware installation, working to drawings and torque specifications.

  • Practical skill in harness work: crimping, soldering, shielding, connector mating and routing.

  • Ability to read and work from mechanical and electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, procedures and work instructions.

  • Experience with electrical verification, including continuity, insulation and short-circuit checks.

  • Understanding of cleanroom, contamination control and ESD requirements.

  • Discipline in documentation and traceability, recording work performed in real time rather than afterwards.

  • Experience raising and documenting non-conformances.

  • Strong communication skills in English (written & spoken).

  • Familiarity with ECSS, NASA or military quality standards.

  • Experience supporting functional test: EGSE connection, test sequence execution and telemetry monitoring.

  • Experience with environmental test campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum) or launch campaigns.

  • Awareness of 6S and good practice in production area organisation.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.



ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.



Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.



YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES 

 


PREPARATION AND READINESS

 - Prepare each operation from the approved procedure, traveller and drawings, and check that the documentation matches the hardware in front of you before starting.

 - Verify hardware before use: part and serial numbers, quantity, physical condition, cleanliness, protections, fasteners and consumables.

 - Prepare and check the tools, torque equipment, MGSE, lifting and handling equipment and integration stands the activity needs.




MECHANICAL AND THERMAL ASSEMBLY AND INTEGRATION

 - Assemble and install satellite structures, panels, brackets, equipment, payloads, mechanisms and thermal hardware to drawing and torque specification.

 - Integrate subsystems into the satellite, verifying fit, alignment and interfaces at each step.

 - Perform handling and lifting operations with MGSE, including satellite rotation, transfer between stands and installation on test adapters.




HARNESS, THERMAL HARDWARE AND MLI

 - Route, install and connect flight harnesses, including crimping, soldering, shielding, connector mating and identification.

 - Perform electrical verification of harnesses, including continuity, insulation and short-circuit checks.

 - Install thermal hardware including heaters, thermistors and thermal interface materials, and fabricate, install and repair multi-layer insulation, including bonding and taping operations.




TEST PREPARATION AND SUPPORT

 - Prepare satellite configurations for functional and environmental testing, including installation on test adapters and mechanical interfaces.

 - Set up and connect EGSE and test benches, support test execution, monitor parameters and report anomalies immediately.

 - Support environmental and launch campaigns on site and off site, including packing, transport preparation and reinstallation.




QUALITY, TRACEABILITY AND NON-CONFORMANCE

 - Record every operation in real time: as-run procedures, logbooks, photographs, and hardware and software configuration, in Manufacturo (MES) and Jira.

 - Perform compliance checks and visual inspections at each critical step, and complete the associated checklists and records.

 - Raise non-conformance reports for any deviation, contribute to first-level investigation, and support root cause analysis and corrective action.




CLEANROOM, SAFETY AND 6S

 - Work to cleanroom, contamination control, ESD, FOD and chemical safety rules, and keep the work area compliant, clean and audit-ready.

 - Maintain 6S in the production stations, and report anything that makes an area unsafe or unfit for flight hardware.




IMPROVEMENT AND TEAM

 - Review work instructions, travellers and checklists against what actually happens on the floor, and give clear feedback so they can be corrected.

 - Support on-the-job training of junior colleagues and share good practice. Senior Technicians coach the team and lead frontline troubleshooting.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR


MUST HAVES:

 - Vocational or technical qualification in mechanical, electrical, electronics, mechatronics or a related field, or equivalent hands-on training.

 - Hands-on experience in the assembly, integration or test of complex electromechanical hardware in satellites. We are hiring at two levels: around 2+ years for Technician, and around 5+ years with demonstrated autonomy for Senior Technician.

 - Practical skill in precision mechanical assembly and thermal hardware installation, working to drawings and torque specifications.

 - Practical skill in harness work: crimping, soldering, shielding, connector mating and routing.

 - Ability to read and work from mechanical and electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, procedures and work instructions.

 - Experience with electrical verification, including continuity, insulation and short-circuit checks.

 - Understanding of cleanroom, contamination control and ESD requirements.

 - Discipline in documentation and traceability, recording work performed in real time rather than afterwards.

 - Experience raising and documenting non-conformances.

 - Comfortable using an MES and Jira for work records. We use Manufacturo and Jira; experience with equivalent systems is fine.

 - Hands-on mindset with strong attention to detail, and the judgement to stop and ask rather than proceed on an assumption.

 - Strong communication skills in English (written & spoken).




NICE TO HAVES:

 - Experience on flight hardware in a satellite or other space environment.

 - Multi-layer insulation fabrication and installation experience.

 - Familiarity with workmanship standards such as IPC-A-610, IPC J-STD-001, IPC-7711/7721 or IPC/WHMA-A-620.

 - Familiarity with ECSS, NASA or military quality standards.

 - Experience supporting functional test: EGSE connection, test sequence execution and telemetry monitoring.

 - Experience with environmental test campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum) or launch campaigns.

 - Awareness of 6S and good practice in production area organisation.




APPLICATION PROCESS

 - Talent Acquisition Interview

 - Hiring Manager General Interview

 - Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge

 - Leadership & Hiring Team Interview




WORKING AT ICEYE

At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.




HOW WE WORK (OUR VALUES)

Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.

 - Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.

 - See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.

 - Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

 - Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

 - Have fun:  What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.
   


BENEFITS

Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing, at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.

Base salary range for this position is dependent on experience, and will be negotiated individually.




OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION

We want ICEYE to be a place where people can be themselves and do great work. Different backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, which is why we work to create an environment where people feel included, respected, and able to speak up. Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table.

We’re committed to fair, inclusive hiring and equal opportunity. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, tell us—we’ll do our best to help.

Apply now to start your ICEYE journey, and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at iceye.com http://iceye.com.

Role highlights:

  • Title: AIT Engineer - Electronics

  • Department: Global Manufacturing Organisation

  • Location: Greece

  • Reporting to: AIT Engineering Team Leader

  • Type of Contract: Permanent

  • Working model: On-site (occasional travel for environmental test and launch campaigns)

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required).

Why this role matters:

The Electronics AIT Engineer transforms satellite electrical designs into reliable, flight-ready hardware. You are the technical authority for electrical and electronic hardware in Athens: how the satellite is wired and connected, what proves it works, and what evidence exists that every build was done correctly.

You own the integration readiness of the electrical subsystems, define the AIT processes, test means and ground support equipment the facilities need, and make sure the design, the processes and the tooling can carry production to high throughput. You also feed what you learn on the floor back into design, so that each build is more manufacturable, more testable and more reliable than the last.

Who We Are


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

Your day-to-day responsibilities

 

AIT Process Definition and Industrialisation

  • Define the electrical MAITE processes for building sub-assemblies and satellites: integration flows, standard sequences, work packages and test strategy.

  • Qualify the critical electrical integration and test processes, and define the acceptance criteria and standardised procedures that go with them.

  • Specify the test means, tooling and workstations each process needs, anticipating them ahead of programme milestones, and lead the transfer from prototype to series so that processes and tooling can carry production to high throughput.

Design Maturity and Co-Engineering

  • Work with Engineering from the concept phase so that design and production constraints are aligned, applying design for manufacturing, assembly and testability (DFM, DFA, DFT) and bringing harness routing, connector access, test points and diagnostic provisions into internal design iterations before the design is frozen.

  • Support internal and supplier design and readiness reviews (e.g. PDR, CDR, PRR, IRR, TRR), ensuring designs are mature and ready for transition into production, and identify industrial risks early with the action plans that close them.

Electrical Integration and Assembly

  • Own the integration readiness of the satellite electrical subsystems, including avionics, power, data handling and communications.

  • Lead and execute electrical integration of satellites and sub-assemblies: harness routing and connection, electrical and RF connections, connector handling, grounding and bonding.

  • Own the electrical build standard, including crimping and soldering practice, connector identification, continuity and insulation verification, cleanliness and ESD discipline.

  • Perform and oversee in-house PCB assembly and rework according to defined work packages and workmanship standards.

  • Verify electronic assemblies before integration and support the floor hands-on during build, connection and test setup.

Functional and Environmental Test

  • Plan, prepare and lead functional, interface and performance test campaigns at subsystem and satellite level, and support the electrical side of environmental campaigns including EMC, thermal vacuum and vibration.

  • Develop and maintain automated and semi-automated test scripts, and monitor telemetry and telecommand during test execution.

  • Act as first responder for electrical anomalies during integration and test, performing initial diagnosis with laboratory instruments and taking findings to root cause.

Electrical Ground Support Equipment

  • Specify, design, procure and validate Electrical Ground Support Equipment and flatsat configurations required for functional and environmental testing.

  • Define the setup, configuration and validation requirements for EGSE, and verify it before use on flight hardware.

Supplier Parts and Electronic Assemblies

  • Act as the technical authority for electronic parts and assemblies from suppliers, covering capability assessment, special process review and First Article Inspection.

  • Define the inspections and workmanship criteria required to verify electronic assemblies, harnesses and PCBAs.

Configuration, Documentation and Anomalies

  • Maintain as-built electrical configuration and traceability, including hardware and software versions, and apply engineering changes consistently to hardware and documentation.

  • Troubleshoot and resolve integration issues, and support root cause analysis and corrective actions, coordinating with the Engineering team, the production team and any other team needed to ensure schedule and quality adherence.

Facilities and Process Requirements

  • Define the electrical AIT process requirements for the facilities and work with the Global Manufacturing Infrastructure team on the layout, power, grounding and test provisions that support them.

  • Define the ESD and handling requirements that electrical integration and test activities must meet, and propose improvements where the process or the environment falls short.

Standardization and Continuous Improvement

  • Capture lessons learned from the floor to improve procedures, test means, test efficiency and build reliability as production volumes increase, and align with the Global AIT and Engineering teams on product standards and process updates.

  • Train and mentor local engineers and technicians on electrical integration and test, fostering a culture of quality and accountability.

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Telecommunications, Aerospace Engineering or a related field.

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in the integration, testing or production of complex electronic hardware systems (e.g. aerospace, defense, automotive, semiconductors, satellites), including work on flight or equivalently critical hardware.

  • Demonstrated experience defining and qualifying electrical integration and test processes, turning them into standardised work packages, and taking a product from first units towards series production.

  • Deep technical knowledge in electronics, with system-level understanding across full product architectures and the ability to spot issues across the interfaces between design, production and operations.

  • Demonstrated ownership of functional and electrical test campaigns, from specification through execution to reporting.

  • Practical mastery of electrical integration: harness routing and connection, crimping and soldering practice, connector identification, continuity and insulation verification.

  • Working knowledge of satellite power subsystems, including batteries, power distribution and the handling and safety constraints that come with them, sufficient to integrate and test them on flight hardware.

  • Experience specifying, designing or validating EGSE or comparable test equipment.

  • Proficiency developing and executing automated or semi-automated test scripts (Python or equivalent).

  • Hands-on troubleshooting of complex electronic systems with laboratory instruments, and the ability to read electrical schematics, interface control documents and technical specifications.

  • Strong track record of enabling design for manufacturing, assembly and testability (DFM, DFA, DFT), working alongside design teams rather than after them.

  • Familiarity with verification and configuration management in complex hardware industries, including root cause analysis and non-conformance ownership through to closure.

  • Working knowledge of cleanroom and ESD discipline. Integration in Athens is typically ISO 8, with ISO 7 and ISO 5 environments also possible.

  • Experience in multidisciplinary engineering environments, mentoring engineers or technicians, and communicating clearly with designers, production leads and executive stakeholders.

  • Strong communication skills in English (written & spoken).

Nice to haves:

  • Familiarity with electronics workmanship standards: IPC-A-610, IPC/WHMA-A-620, J-STD-001.

  • Familiarity with EN 9100 and ECSS standards as applied to space hardware.

  • RF integration and test experience, including connector care, cable loss and measurement practice.

  • Embedded systems and hardware interfaces (SPI, UART, I2C, CAN, Ethernet), and familiarity with Linux.

  • Experience supporting environmental test campaigns from the electrical side (EMC, thermal vacuum, vibration).

  • Familiarity with PLM, ERP, Manufacturo (MES) or Jira for build records and configuration control.

  • Launch campaign experience.

Application Process

  • Talent Acquisition Interview

  • Hiring Manager General Interview

  • Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge

  • Leadership & Hiring Team Interview

Working at ICEYE

At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.

Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.

  • Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.

  • See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.

  • Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

  • Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

  • Have fun: What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing, at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.

Base salary range for this position is dependent on experience, and will be negotiated individually.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

Role highlights:

  • Senior Cloud Network Engineer

  • Location: Espoo, Finland or Berlin, Germany

  • Department: Product Networking

  • Reports to: Engineering Manager

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Workplace model: Hybrid (3 days per week in office)

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

ICEYE's satellite operations, ground systems and customer deliveries depend on cloud and hybrid networks that have to hold up when it matters most. You'll be one of the go-to experts for how those networks are architected in AWS and connected to the rest of our infrastructure, leading the subsystems you own and shaping how the team builds them. Few network engineers get to work on infrastructure like this.

  • Design and evolve ICEYE's AWS network architecture, including VPCs, Transit Gateways, Direct Connects and VPN connectivity

  • Connect cloud environments securely to ground stations, data centers and on-premises sites

  • Manage cloud network infrastructure as code with Terraform and version-controlled change through CI/CD

  • Act as a go-to expert for deep network issues in production, and put patterns and guardrails in place that prevent them from coming back

  • Shape how the team designs, reviews and documents network changes, with the impact on other teams in mind

  • Own critical production systems with a focus on reliability, observability and security against real-world threats

Must haves:

  • A solid network engineering foundation built in data center, service provider or enterprise network environments

  • Extensive hands-on experience designing and operating network architecture in AWS, including VPCs, Transit Gateways, Direct Connects and VPNs

  • Strong experience with BGP and routing across hybrid cloud and on-premises environments

  • Infrastructure as code for networking with Terraform, Git and CI/CD pipelines

  • Experience with secure network design, including firewalling, segmentation and zero trust access

  • Ability to lead network architecture decisions and to explain and defend the trade-offs with peers

  • Pragmatic, collaborative mindset with the ability to balance technical quality with business needs


Nice to haves:

  • Software development experience, especially for network applications and automation (for example Python or Go)

  • Strong Linux networking skills

  • TA Partner Screen Call

  • Hiring Manager Interview

  • Technical Interview

  • Values & Fit Interview

  • SVP of Engineering Interview

As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one.   • Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

  • Have fun: What we do matters, and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.


Benefits

  • Satellite Operations Specialist

  • Location: Finland

  • Department: Satellite Operations & Maintenance / Engineering

  • Reports to: Satellite Operations Team Lead

  • Employment type: Fixed term

  • Workplace model: Office

  • Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

 

Why this role matters:

 

As a Satellite Operations Specialist, you will be an integral part of ensuring that ICEYE is able to deliver the product and data to customers. You will work closely with other operators on the operations console throughout your shift hours, ensuring smooth operation of our constellation of satellites and providing crucial support for any unexpected contingencies that arise on the fleet or ground systems. You will help to improve Satellite Operations by developing new procedures and tools. You'll handle fleet maintenance, engage in mock operations pre-launch, and be a critical part of the Launch and Early Orbit Operations. If you're passionate about space technology and eager to make an impact in satellite operations, we want to hear from you.

 

Who We Are

 

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE’s world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world’s largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy – day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

 

As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE’s near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring (including oil-spill detection), and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.

 

ICEYE is headquartered in Finland and operates globally across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We have more than 900 employees, united by a shared vision: improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.


Your day-to-day responsibilities

 

  • Maintain continuous, high-quality monitoring and control of the satellite constellation during all shifts

  • Ensure safe operations, early detection of anomalies, and proper escalation or resolution

  • Enhance Satellite Operations by developing and refining procedures, tools, and workflow

  • Support fleet maintenance activities and satellite in orbit testing

  • Contribute to mission readiness through simulations and Launch and Early Orbit Operations

  • Deliver clear shift handovers, incident reporting, and documentation

  • Contribute to seamless 24/7 operations and strengthen team-wide situational awareness and best practices.

 

What we’re looking for

 

Must haves:

  • Relevant university degree: Aeronautical Engineering, Space studies, Applied Physics or similar, or relative experience in a similar role.

  • Have attention to detail with an excellent ability to focus

  • Have strong problem-solving skills and the ability to react fast

  • Strong English language skills (both written and spoken)

  • Flexibility in scheduled working hours (ability to work morning, evening, and night shifts, 365/24/7 basis)

  • Interest in Space Industry/Satellite Operations

 

Nice to haves:

  • Space background

  • Knowledge about satellite systems

  • Knowledge about orbital mechanics

  • Familiarity with Linux system

  • Familiarity with Python

  • Familiarity with Atlassian Cloud (Jira, Confluence)

 

Application Process

 

  • Talent Attraction Partner interview (30 minutes, online)

  • Technical / Team Lead interview (30 minutes, online)

  • Team Director interview (30 minutes, online)

 

Working at ICEYE

 

At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority—with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.

  • Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.

  • Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.

  • See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.

  • Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

  • Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

  • Have fun: What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.

  • Location: Portugal

  • Department: Mission Sales

  • Reports to: VP Missions Sales Spain & Portugal, dotted line to CEO Portugal

  • Workplace model: Hybrid (Lisbon office)

We are looking for someone analytical and paranoid about disciplined sales execution: every opportunity qualified, every follow-up on time, every record accurate.

You will work closely with the VP, Missions Sales Spain & Portugal as a trusted partner in day-to-day commercial execution, with dotted-line collaboration with the ICEYE Portugal CEO to ensure strong local alignment. By helping manage customer engagement, regional opportunities, events, and cross-functional collaboration, you will directly support ICEYE’s ambition to become the global provider of turnkey ISR infrastructure to allied nations. While Missions is your line of business, you represent ICEYE as a single company: you quickly identify opportunities outside Missions – satellite data, analytics solutions – follow up on them, and connect them to the right ICEYE teams.

  • Engage with government, defence, space, and industry dual-use stakeholders, end-users, including ministries of defence, space agencies, ESA-related stakeholders, primes, associations, and commercial partners.

  • Support the VP, Missions Sales Spain & Portugal with customer follow-up, meeting preparation, opportunity tracking, and regional account activity.

  • Maintain accurate and timely Campaign plans and Salesforce records, including pipeline updates, meeting notes, next steps, and opportunity status. Run a disciplined execution cadence: no stale opportunities, no missed follow-ups.

  • Quickly identify and follow up on opportunities outside the Missions line of business (e.g., satellite data and analytics solutions), and bring in the right ICEYE teams so nothing is dropped – ensuring customers always experience ICEYE as one company.

  • Work closely with Sales Engineering and other internal experts to support bids, proposals, customer presentations, and technical-commercial responses.

  • Help coordinate ICEYE’s Portugal commercial presence at regional events, sectorial associations, regional or local exhibitions, industry forums, and customer-facing activities.

  • Collaborate with Marketing, Data, Missions, and other teams to ensure joined-up customer engagement and strong regional positioning.

  • Share market intelligence, customer feedback, and competitor insights to support regional planning and prioritisation.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience in business development, sales, account management, or capture within defence, aerospace, space, ISR, NATO, or other high-technology environments.

  • Experience working with both government/public-sector customers and commercial or industry partners.

  • Familiarity with the defence and space ecosystem in Portugal, including relevant government bodies, agencies, primes, integrators, or industry associations.

  • Experience using Salesforce or other CRM systems to manage opportunities in a structured way, including lead qualification, stakeholder mapping, follow-up, pipeline tracking, and cross-functional coordination.

  • Analytical by default: you build the territory and account case with data, qualify rigorously, and are paranoid about disciplined sales execution.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively across commercial, technical, marketing, and leadership teams.

  • Professional fluency in Portuguese and English.

  • Willingness to travel regularly across Portugal, Finland or other ICEYE locations.

  • Experience supporting bids, tenders, capture plans, gate reviews, or proposal development.

Nice to haves:

  • Previous military, government, or defence-sector experience.

  • Exposure to earth observation, satellite systems, or defence intelligence solutions.

  • Existing network across ministries of defence, space agencies, ESA-related stakeholders, local primes, or defence and space associations.

  • Experience applying GenAI or AI-enabled tooling to business development, sales, market intelligence, CRM hygiene, proposal preparation, stakeholder mapping, or other commercial workflows.

  • Sales training in Miller Heiman, Korn Ferry, Shipley or similar.

• Mission Delivery Engineer

  • Department: Missions Line of Business

  • Location: ICEYE Lisbon, Portugal

  • Reports to: VP of Program Management, dotted line to Portugal CEO

  • Employment type: Permanent

  • Working type: Hybrid (3 days / week in office)

  • Must be eligible and able to attain relevant national and NATO security clearances

Why this role matters

As a Missions Delivery Engineer you will support the delivery of complex Satellite Mission programs end-to-end with deep technical ownership, ensuring customer success, on-time execution, and scalable delivery excellence.

You will work across the Portuguese Portfolio focusing on the technical thread of customer missions—from requirements capture through system acceptance and delivery—acting as the technical authority/interface between the customer and ICEYE's engineering, product, and operations teams. Your role bridges program governance and system engineering: ensuring mission requirements are understood, flowed down, tracked, and validated, while maintaining configuration control and driving cross-functional technical alignment throughout the program lifecycle.

This role directly contributes to ICEYE's ambition to become the leading provider of space-based ISR infrastructure by scaling reliable, high-impact mission delivery globally.

The role will be based in Lisbon at the ICEYE facility. Travel to customer sites is required.

• Customer technical requirements are accurately captured, baselined, and flowed down to engineering teams, ensuring all mission commitments are fully traceable from contract to delivery.

• Customers experience a consistent, high-trust technical partnership, with a single accountable interface that understands their systems and operational needs throughout the program lifecycle.

• System integration, verification, and validation activities are planned and executed rigorously, ensuring all delivered capabilities are compliant with mission and contractual requirements.

• Configuration and interface control is maintained across all mission segments—satellite, ground, networks, and user interfaces—minimising risk from upgrades, changes, and inter-system dependencies.

• Technical risks, discrepancies, and gaps are identified early, escalated effectively and resolved proactively through structured coordination across software, hardware, operations, and QA teams.

• Cross-functional technical teams operate in alignment, with clear ownership and system-level perspective maintained across all reviews, delivery milestones, and readiness checks.

• Technical documentation—including CONOPS, ICDs, verification matrices, mission analysis, and acceptance reports—is delivered on time and kept current with the actual system implementation.

• 5+ years' experience delivering complex, multi-stakeholder technical programs in advanced technology environments (e.g. space, defence, telecom, automotive, IT)

• Proven ability to own the technical customer interface, managing senior stakeholders and translating operational requirements into engineering deliverables

• Hands-on experience with requirements management, traceability, and configuration control across hardware, software, and system-level domains

• Demonstrated involvement in system integration, verification and validation (V&V) planning and execution, including acceptance testing campaigns

• Strong cross-functional technical coordination skills across engineering, product, and operations disciplines

• Experience of carrying out analysis and mission design using software packages such as STK, SaVoir, MONTE or GMAT

• Excellent communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences, including formal reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, DRR)

• Degree in engineering, systems engineering, computer science, or a related technical field

• Must have or be able to obtain required security clearances

• Experience in Earth Observation (EO), SAR, or remote sensing

• Background in space mission systems or satellite ground segment development

• Experience working with government or defence customers on classified or sovereign programs

• Knowledge of hardware/software integration, API control, and embedded systems

• Familiarity with ESA or equivalent program documentation frameworks

• Advanced degree (Master's) or relevant certifications (e.g. PMP, PgMP, INCOSE CSEP)

• Cross-functional technical teams operate in alignment, with clear ownership and system-level perspective maintained across all reviews, delivery milestones, and readiness checks.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

• 5+ years' experience delivering complex, multi-stakeholder technical programs in advanced technology environments (e.g. space, defence, telecom, automotive, IT)

• Experience of carrying out analysis and mission design using software packages such as STK, SaVoir, MONTE or GMAT

• Degree in engineering, systems engineering, computer science, or a related technical field

• Must have or be able to obtain required security clearances

• Experience in Earth Observation (EO), SAR, or remote sensing

• Background in space mission systems or satellite ground segment development

• Experience working with government or defence customers on classified or sovereign programs

• Knowledge of hardware/software integration, API control, and embedded systems

• Familiarity with ESA or equivalent program documentation frameworks

• Advanced degree (Master's) or relevant certifications (e.g. PMP, PgMP, INCOSE CSEP)

• Initial screening call with Talent Attraction

• Hiring Manager interview with Mission Program Director
